questions.text: A company is designing global inbound content distribution design. The requirement is low latency, high availability, and clear operational ownership. Which design should the network specialist recommend?

answers.text: CloudFront or Global Accelerator selected according to cacheability, protocol, static IP, failover, and origin-protection requirements
Rely on default BGP timers for sub-second failover detection
Use VPC interface endpoints to expose your services to the public internet
Use NAT gateway in every private subnet to maximize redundancy and minimize latency

explanations.a: CloudFront or Global Accelerator selected according to cacheability, protocol, static IP, failover, and origin-protection requirements is appropriate for global inbound content distribution design. It matches the traffic pattern and avoids adding unrelated control planes.
explanations.b: Default BGP timers detect failure in tens of seconds; BFD is needed for sub-second.
explanations.c: Interface endpoints provide private connectivity into AWS; public exposure uses ALB/NLB or PrivateLink-as-provider.
explanations.d: One NAT gateway per AZ is the recommended pattern; per-subnet NAT inflates cost without resilience benefit.

questions.name: Network Design
questions.text: An application migration depends on multi-Region multi-account routing architecture. The target architecture requires controlled failover and predictable traffic paths during impairment. Which design decision is correct?

answers.text: Configure jumbo frames on a Site-to-Site VPN tunnel
Skip IaC and rely on point-in-time AWS Console screenshots for repeatability
Move all viewer traffic through a single Region for global low latency
Regional transit hubs, inter-Region peering, centralized inspection, controlled route propagation, shared services placement, and onboarding governance

explanations.a: AWS Site-to-Site VPN does not support jumbo frames; MTU is fixed with extra IPsec overhead.
explanations.b: Screenshots cannot be replayed and do not capture dependencies; IaC is the supported path.
explanations.c: Single-Region routing forces long round trips for distant users; CloudFront/Global Accelerator distribute closer.
explanations.d: Regional transit hubs, inter-Region peering, centralized inspection, controlled route propagation, shared services placement, and onboarding governance is appropriate for multi-Region multi-account routing architecture. It reduces unnecessary exposure while preserving the required connectivity behavior.
